content.text:
You are picking up four open problems from a feature called "print issues" in JusPrin, a fork of OrcaSlicer (C++17, wxWidgets, OpenGL). Investigate each and write a proposal with evidence. Do not ship fixes without Kenneth's approval; a small isolated prototype to prove a point is fine.

## Where the work is

- Repository: /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin. Production branch: `jusprin-newui`.
- The feature is UNCOMMITTED in the git worktree `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/wonderful-roentgen-83d009` (branch `claude/persistent-print-issues-spike-9238a1`). Another session owns that worktree. Do NOT work in it, build in it, or check anything out there. Read its files freely. If you need to run code, create your own worktree and copy the uncommitted changes into it (`git -C <that worktree> diff` plus the untracked files listed by `git -C <that worktree> status --short`), or wait until Kenneth has committed the feature and branch from that commit. Ask Kenneth which he prefers if it matters.
- Read first: `AGENTS.md`, then in `agent-docs/jusprin/` of that worktree: `architecture.md` (section "Print issues"), `orca-integration-guide.md` (section "Print problems are read back from OrcaSlicer, not recorded as they pass"), and `fork-stewardship.md` (required before touching any OrcaSlicer-owned file: every upstream line changed is re-resolved at every rebase; run the merge simulation it describes and report both endpoint commits).
- Background report with measurements: `investigation-persistent-print-issues-run2.md` in that worktree's root (untracked on purpose; never commit it or hide it with ignore rules).

## What the feature does

Inside the JusPrin shell, OrcaSlicer's own pop-up notices (the stack in the lower right corner of the 3D view) are no longer drawn. Instead:

- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrintIssues/PrintIssueMonitor.{hpp,cpp}` builds a list of current print problems for the active plate by re-asking OrcaSlicer's own public checks and reading state OrcaSlicer already stores. It contains no rule of its own about what is a problem. Sources it reads today: `Print::validate` (one error and one warning at most), a copy straddling the plate edge (`ModelInstance::print_volume_state`), a filament its nozzle cannot reach (via `GLCanvas3D::check_volumes_outside_state`), the plate checks `PartPlate::check_tpu_printable_status`, `check_filament_printable`, `check_mixture_of_pla_and_petg`, `check_compatible_of_nozzle_and_filament`, `check_mixture_filament_compatible`, prime tower outside the plate, slicing step warnings (`step_state_with_warnings`), the slice result (path conflict, G-code processor warnings, toolpath outside the build volume, `gcode_check_result`, `filament_printable_reuslt`), and the reason a slice failed (captured from `EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED`).
- `PrintIssues/IssueOverlay.{hpp,cpp}` draws a status pill in the lower right corner of the Prepare canvas, a list, and a bubble beside the affected object with "Ask AI" and "Resolve with AI". Layout rules are in `PrintIssues/IssueOverlayLayout.{hpp,cpp}`.
- The only upstream edit is two added lines in `src/slic3r/GUI/NotificationManager.cpp`, inside `render_notifications`, after `sort_notifications()`: it returns early when `wxGetApp().plater()->get_view3D_canvas3D()->legacy_overlays_hidden()` is true. That flag is one the shell already sets on install and restores when the person switches back to the stock ("classic") presentation. Only drawing stops: notices are still pushed, timed out and closed, because that lifecycle runs in `NotificationManager::update_notifications`.
- Tests: `tests/shell/print_issues_scenario.inc` (run with the shell harness, `--print-issues` or `--print-issues-capture <dir>`; build target `shell_integration_harness`), `tests/jusprin/test_print_issues.cpp`, and the "[print-issues]" cases at the end of `tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp`.

Kenneth decided to hide ALL native notices. The four problems below are the cost of that decision.

## Problem 1: operation notices are gone with no replacement

The same notification manager also carries notices that are not print problems, and hiding everything hides them too: export finished (with "open folder" and "eject"), upload-to-printer and download progress, update available, network and sync errors (including a sync conflict notice with its own action buttons), tips, and the object-size card. Slicing progress and its cancel action are still available in the JusPrin header. The full list of kinds is the `NotificationType` enum in `src/slic3r/GUI/NotificationManager.hpp`.

Deliver: an inventory of every `NotificationType` with who pushes it, whether it is a one-time event or a lasting state, whether it carries an action (a hypertext callback or buttons), and whether JusPrin already shows the same fact somewhere (header, chat, Home). Then a proposal for where each kind that matters should appear in JusPrin and by what mechanism. Note the key difficulty: print problems are states that can be re-asked from OrcaSlicer, but these are events with nothing to re-ask, so they need to be captured as they are pushed. The fork already has one hook at the single insertion point (`report_file_load_message` in `NotificationManager::push_notification_data`, see `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/FileLoads.hpp`); evaluate whether that seam can be generalised with little or no extra upstream footprint. The product definition (`agent-docs/jusprin/product-definition.md`) says which surfaces must remain; the original handoff required keeping operation failures out of the print-readiness list.

## Problem 2: "flushing volume set to 0" is not covered

OrcaSlicer warns "Partial flushing volume set to 0. Multi-color printing may cause color mixing in models." The check is `GLCanvas3D::is_flushing_matrix_error()` in `src/slic3r/GUI/GLCanvas3D.cpp`, which is private, so the monitor cannot call it and this warning is now shown nowhere. Options to compare with measured upstream cost: make that one function public (a one-word upstream change; measure upstream history at that line), find another public route to the same fact, or read the notice's presence from the notification manager. Do not copy the check's logic into fork code: duplicated logic drifts from upstream silently.

## Problem 3: new warning kinds from upstream will be invisible

A warning OrcaSlicer adds in a future version is drawn nowhere until someone writes a reader for it, and nothing fails to tell us. Propose a guard. Ideas to evaluate, not a prescribed answer: (a) a catch-all reader over the notification manager's current warning- and error-level notices for kinds no specific reader claims, shown as plate-wide issues with OrcaSlicer's raw text (needs a small read accessor on `NotificationManager`, an upstream edit, so measure it; note that with drawing suppressed nobody can dismiss a notice, which removes the main weakness of reading notices); (b) a test that fails when `NotificationType` or `GLCanvas3D::EWarning` gains a value the fork has not classified; (c) a check run after each upstream rebase. Two notification kinds are shared between sources, which limits filtering by kind: "SlicingError" is used for slice failures and for canvas errors such as toolpath out of bounds, and "PlaterError" for an object over the plate edge and at least one other producer in `Plater.cpp` (around the call to `push_plater_error_notification` near the mesh-combining code). Identity must never be derived from message text.

## Problem 4: the new readers were never triggered at runtime

The readers added for the plate checks and post-slice checks compile and were reviewed against OrcaSlicer's code, but none of their conditions was reproduced, because the harness's test printer has one nozzle and no TPU. Unverified today: two or more TPU filaments, filament not printable, PLA mixed with PETG, nozzle and filament incompatible, filament mixture incompatible, prime tower outside the plate, a filament its nozzle cannot reach (left/right nozzle), toolpath outside the plate, toolpath above the print height, nozzle printable-area and printable-height errors after slicing, and filament not printable on the plate surface. Also never reproduced: a slicing failure that names its object, and G-code processor warnings.

Deliver: for each, a reproduction recipe in the real app (which printer profile, filaments, model, and steps), and where feasible a new step in `tests/shell/print_issues_scenario.inc` that produces it through native paths and checks the monitor reports it with the right severity and target. A dual-nozzle Bambu profile (H2D) and multi-filament setups are likely needed; `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` describes the in-process fake Bambu printer. For any reader whose text the fork composes from OrcaSlicer's translation strings (the nozzle range and height sentences in `PrintIssueMonitor::collect_result`), compare the result with what OrcaSlicer's own notice says in the stock presentation and report differences. Mark anything you cannot reproduce as unverified; do not fill gaps with plausible explanations.

## Ground rules (Kenneth's)

- Never apply a fix for something you have not reproduced. Search and verify before asserting; label inference as inference.
- Test end to end in the local dev environment. The harness needs a scratch `HOME`; never drive or kill another JusPrin instance on the machine. Build recipe and traps are in the saved notes for this project (worktree build, llvm-ar for the 4 GiB archive, absolute build paths).
- Keep temporary reports untracked and visible; do not commit them.
- Commit only when Kenneth asks.

Hand back one short report: per problem, the recommendation, the evidence, the upstream footprint with merge-simulation results where an upstream edit is proposed, and the decisions Kenneth has to make.

input.command: cd /Users/kenneth/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/memory/ && cat persistent-print-issues-spike.md jusprin-worktree-build.md liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit.md never-reuse-another-sessions-worktree.md worktree-session-cannot-write-main-checkout.md investigation-report-four-part-frame.md harness-gl-readback-capture.md fake-bambu-printer-sim.md background-bash-timeout-kills-builds.md bash-cwd-resets-after-background.md workspace-harness-never-post-inits-on-mac.md live-test-built-app-on-mac.md

---
name: persistent-print-issues-spike
description: "2026-10-08 second-run spike: print issues outside chat work with zero upstream edits; where the prototype and report live, the native facts that shaped it, and the decisions still open"
metadata:
  type: project
---

Second run of the "persistent print issues" spike (2026-10-08). Kenneth called the first run (Codex, `investigation-persistent-print-issues.md` in the main checkout, producer hooks in Plater.cpp) "really bad" without saying why, and asked for an independent redo with a prototype pre-approved.

**Where it lives:** uncommitted in worktree `.claude/worktrees/wonderful-roentgen-83d009` (branch `claude/persistent-print-issues-spike-9238a1`). Report: `investigation-persistent-print-issues-run2.md` there, evidence in the folder of the same name. Code: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrintIssues/` (PrintIssueMonitor, IssueOverlay), `AgentHost::submit_issue_message`, harness modes `--print-issues`, `--print-issues-capture <dir>`, `--manual-print-issues`.

**Result:** end to end works with 0 lines changed in OrcaSlicer-owned files for the feature itself. The reader re-asks native checks instead of recording at producers.

**2026-10-09: converted to production work by Kenneth** ("ignore everything that said this is a temporary spike"). His decisions: hide ALL native notices; status pill in the canvas's lower right corner (where notices were), list opening upward; chat message quotes Orca's text. Upstream footprint is 2 added lines in `NotificationManager::render_notifications`: an early return when `wxGetApp().plater()->get_view3D_canvas3D()->legacy_overlays_hidden()` (Kenneth's idea: reuse the flag the shell already sets and restores; my first version added a 6-line dedicated switch). It asks the Prepare canvas, not the drawn canvas, because Check print is a second canvas without the flag and drew the notices again (tested). It sits after `sort_notifications()` because current upstream added `m_imgui_ready = true` at the top of the function (the merge simulation caught that). With no agent set up, a press sends nothing and a dialog offers setup (Kenneth's decision, 2026-10-09). A task chip was spawned for the four gaps hiding all notices leaves (operation notices, flushing-volume warning, future upstream warning kinds, readers never triggered at runtime). Uncommitted candidate passes: print-issues scenario 39 steps/336 checks in light and dark, shell regression 527, agent_bridge_tests 4756, jusprin_tests 584. Files no longer carry "spike" in their names: `tests/shell/print_issues_scenario.inc`, `print_issues_agent.hpp`, `tests/jusprin/test_print_issues.cpp`.

Kenneth caught by hand that the bubble covered its object near the top edge; 324 green checks had missed it because nothing asserted "does not cover the object". Placement is now `PrintIssues/IssueOverlayLayout` with unit tests.

**Native facts worth not rediscovering:**
- `Print::validate` is public and const; re-calling it on `PartPlate::fff_print()` costs under 1 ms. It holds one error and one warning at most.
- `Plater::is_background_process_update_scheduled()` (public) is true during the 500 ms before Orca applies an edit to the print; that is the "not yet validated" signal.
- `EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED` is defined in Plater.cpp and declared nowhere. A `wxDECLARE_EVENT` in `JusPrin/Workspace/PlaterProjectState.hpp` (pulled into Plater.cpp by the `ProjectState.hpp` shim) gives it external linkage with no upstream edit.
- A copy over the plate edge is dropped from validation. A slice warning stays current after a plain move and goes non-current only when its step is invalidated. A move during a slice does not cancel it.
- Notification popups are not an issue list: dismissal removes them, targets are in closures, and they are not retired while the window is inactive.

**Still open (Kenneth's):** repeat presses; other plates; whether to run a live-model check; a JusPrin surface for operation notices (export finished, upload progress, network errors), which hiding all notices removed.

Related: [[agent-bridge-phase-3]], [[jusprin-chip-orca-seams]], [[fork-rebase-risk-verify-before-claiming]].

name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

name: liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit
description: "RelWithDebInfo liblibslic3r_gui.a crossed Apple ar's 4 GiB archive limit on jusprin-newui (2026-09-13); CMAKE_AR override is ignored; manual llvm-ar relink recipe and its cd trap"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 0771473f-5d46-4419-b8e5-112938ea6b34
  modified: 2026-09-14T14:18:50.456Z
---

On 2026-09-13, at jusprin-newui 770bd2b0a2 (after "Add the evidence-led Add a
printer flow"), a worktree RelWithDebInfo build failed archiving
`src/slic3r/RelWithDebInfo/liblibslic3r_gui.a`:
`Assertion failed: (memberOffset < 0xFFFFFFFF) ... ArchiveWriter.cpp` then
`fatal error in .../ranlib`. The archive llvm-ar produced was 4,309,350,176
bytes; the main checkout's copy built minutes earlier was 4,143,827,796 and
still fit. Objects are big because the root CMakeLists.txt (lines ~544-548)
rewrites RelWithDebInfo -O2 to -O0 on purpose. Disk space was not the cause.

**Why:** the failed build left the OLD harness binary in place, and the harness
runs afterwards "passed" against stale code (a new `--printer-setup` flag
silently ran the default mode: same 285 check count). Gate runs on build
success and compare binary mtime.

**How to apply:**
- `-DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar` on an existing build dir does
  nothing: `CMakeFiles/<ver>/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` sets CMAKE_AR as a normal
  variable that shadows the cache.
- Working relink: `ninja -f build-RelWithDebInfo.ninja -t commands <target>`,
  drop compile lines, swap ar/ranlib for llvm-ar/llvm-ranlib on the gui archive
  line only, then run EACH line in its own `(cd build/arm64 && eval "$line")`.
  One `sh` script fails with bogus "no such file" errors because the
  encoding-check line does `cd src/slic3r` and it leaks; `sh -e` also does not
  stop inside `&&` chains. Apple's linker accepted the >4 GiB llvm-ar archive.
- The fix is PER BUILD DIRECTORY, nothing in the repo selects llvm-ar. Main
  checkout's build/arm64 cache has llvm-ar (commit 449b676145 documents it in
  agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md); any newly configured build dir
  gets Apple ar and fails again. Configure new dirs with the flags in
  [[jusprin-worktree-build]].
- Recurred 2026-09-14 on a fresh worktree at jusprin-newui bc19661a7f (archive
  4,308,513,464 bytes). Shortcut that worked: after the failed build, from
  `-t commands shell_integration_harness` drop lines containing ` -c `; only
  the last two remain relevant (gui archive, then harness link). Run just
  those two, swapping ar/ranlib on the archive line. Harness then passed.
- A lasting fix (llvm-ar in the toolchain, thin archives, or less debug info)
  is Kenneth's call; the main checkout will hit this on its next growth.

Related: [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].

name: never-reuse-another-sessions-worktree
description: "A clean, merged, idle worktree under .claude/worktrees still belongs to its session; its owner can resume and check out over you mid-run. Always create your own."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: cb4c8804-b0a0-4ca0-b4a5-6b6998947d4b
  modified: 2026-09-24T00:36:34.672Z
---

On 2026-09-23 I reused `.claude/worktrees/compassionate-gould-f98259` to skip a full build: it was clean, detached at a commit already merged into jusprin-newui, no process had files open there, and its build dir was only 9 days old. An hour later its owning session resumed, checked out two other branches there (the reflog shows it), rewrote ~13,800 resource files, and my running harness crashed with "Could not load bitmap: bed_high_templ" -- a symptom that looked like a product bug.

**Why:** "clean and idle" says nothing about ownership. The session that created a worktree can resume at any time, and it has no way to know someone else moved in.

**How to apply:** create a new worktree with its own name (`git worktree add -b <branch> .claude/worktrees/<name> <base>`) and configure a fresh build dir with the flags in [[jusprin-worktree-build]]. At jusprin-newui bd8ea51abc a fresh build of `jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs agent_bridge_tests shell_integration_harness` was 881 ninja steps, not the hour I feared. If a harness run dies strangely, check `git -C <worktree> reflog -3 --date=iso` and file mtimes before suspecting the code. Related: [[subagent-worktrees-create-manually]].

On 2026-10-08 a session running in `.claude/worktrees/<name>` tried to write a report next to its handoff in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/` and the Write tool was refused by a hook: edits to the base checkout "do not land on this session's branch and may corrupt the user's primary working copy". Bash `cp` is not stopped by the hook, but that is working around a deliberate guard, so anything copied there was moved back.

**Why:** handoffs are read from the main checkout ([[handoff-docs-not-committed]]), which makes it tempting to hand the report back in the same place.

**How to apply:** write reports and evidence folders in the worktree root, leave them untracked ([[temp-docs-stay-untracked-and-visible]]), and give Kenneth the worktree path. Never use the scratchpad for a deliverable; the app's file pane cannot open it as part of the project.

name: harness-gl-readback-capture
description: "When the Mac screen is locked the shell harness's screen-blit captures come back blank (2.8 KB PNGs); read the canvas's own pixels with glReadPixels(GL_FRONT) after render() instead"
metadata:
  type: reference
---

`write_screen_capture` / `blit_screen` in `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp` photograph the desktop through `wxScreenDC`. With the screen locked (`ioreg -n Root -d1 | grep CGSSessionScreenIsLocked` prints a line) every PNG is a blank ~2.8 KB file and no check fails.

For anything drawn inside the GL canvas (ImGui overlays, the tool strip, bubbles) read the frame back instead: `prepare_canvas().render()`, then `glReadBuffer(GL_FRONT)` and `glReadPixels` over `get_canvas_size()`, flip vertically into a `wxImage`, save as PNG. Worked on 2026-10-08 with the screen locked and the window inactive; needs `#include <glad/gl.h>`. Native notifications drawn by Orca are in the same frame, so they appear too. Web views still need `capture_web_view`.

Side effect of an inactive window: Orca's `NotificationManager::update_notifications` returns early, so closed popups are never retired and `get_notification_count()` only grows.

Related: [[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]], [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[screenshots-to-files-via-page-fixture]].

name: fake-bambu-printer-sim
description: "src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/FakeBambuAgent.{hpp,cpp} — the in-process Bambu printer stand-in that IS on jusprin-newui (unlike the Moonraker simulator); keeps a real Bambu system preset selected and substitutes only the agent."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: b5985db0-8e89-40a4-b560-5b7dcd439f2d
  modified: 2026-09-16T15:54:40.830Z
---

`jusprin-newui` (the current working branch as of 2026-09-16) carries an in-process fake Bambu printer, landed as two commits: `7acf075aaa` (implementation, 2026-09-08 10:57) and `e04c0d40d3` (docs, 2026-09-08 11:00). Both are `Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>` — done by a Cursor agent on worktree branch `cursor/cd073db7` (created from `a9adaae973`), then cherry-picked onto `jusprin-newui` (parent `367f5703b3`). Operator guide: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md`.

**Design:** unlike the Moonraker simulator ([[fake-moonraker-printer-sim]], which fakes the wire protocol and lives on a different branch entirely), this keeps a real Bambu Lab **system** preset selected (so `PresetBundle::is_bbl_vendor()` stays true and every Bambu-only UI gate passes) and substitutes only the printer-agent implementation, at the `NetworkAgentFactory` factory level, under id `jusprin-fake-bambu`. Two earlier attempts (`a162493544`, `3c244108b4`, both reverted same day) tried faking a *non-Bambu* agent or patching the header chip directly — both failed because Bambu-only gates rejected them or because it only patched a symptom. Faking Bambu's real network (MQTT/TLS 8883, FTPS 990, discovery) was evaluated and explicitly rejected as out of scope.

**The seam:** exactly 4 added lines in `GUI_App::switch_printer_agent` (`src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_App.cpp:3574-3579`, 1 include + 3 body lines) — inside the existing `if (preset_bundle->is_bbl_vendor())` branch, `fake_bambu_printer_agent_id(app_config)` overrides `effective_agent_id` when fake mode is on, otherwise the branch is untouched. No upstream line deleted.

**Config surface is a JSON file only, no MCP tools** (Kenneth's explicit call): turn it on via `"jusprin": {"fake_printer": true}` in `JusPrin2.conf` (JSON booleans store as the string `"true"`; an INI `[jusprin]` block is silently ignored), then drive live state by writing `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` (reread ~1s) with `state`/`progress`/`nozzle`/`bed`/`offline` keys. The C++ parameter carrying the datadir into the agent is misleadingly named `log_dir` (an upstream `NetworkAgentFactory::PrinterAgentFactory` convention, documented as "Directory for log files") — verified it's actually `data_dir()` at the call site, not a log subdirectory; don't be misled by the name when reading the code.

Emulates printer type `N1` (`JUSPRIN_FAKE_BAMBU_PRINTER_TYPE`), device id `FAKE001`, shows as **JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)** in Select Machine. Idle/Printing/Offline is the printer-menu **first row** (opened by clicking the printer half of the chip), never on the chip itself. The heartbeat thread does not start in the constructor — only in `set_queue_on_main_fn` when a real callback is set — so unit tests that never wire that callback stay quiet. Test target: `jusprin_fake_bambu_tests` (`tests/jusprin/test_fake_bambu_agent.cpp`), coexists with `shell_theme_tests` in the same CMakeLists (their merge was a conflict the cherry-pick resolved by keeping both).

Doc pointers added in the two landing commits: `AGENTS.md`, `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md`, `agent-docs/jusprin/engineering-method.md` ("Printer tests without hardware" section), `agent-docs/jusprin/orca-integration-guide.md`. A planning handoff doc (`agent-docs/jusprin/fake-bambu-printer-handoff.md`) was never committed and doesn't exist in the tree — don't look for it.

**Why:** Kenneth wants Bambu-path testing (header menu state, Select Machine, print job) without hardware, on the branch he actually works on day to day — distinct from the Moonraker/Klipper simulator, which stays on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` and covers the print-host HTTP path instead.

**How to apply:** For "fake a printer on jusprin-newui" requests, this is the one that's actually there — check `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/` first. name: background-bash-timeout-kills-builds
description: "A run_in_background Bash build dies at the tool timeout (ninja prints \"interrupted by user\", exit 130); launch long builds with nohup and watch the log instead"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 8c1e8dd3-1475-48e9-9398-2d5eaa424bab
  modified: 2026-09-14T19:01:34.576Z
---

A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

description: "The Bash tool's working directory silently reverts to the primary repo after a run_in_background command or a failed cd; worktree commands must cd explicitly or use absolute paths."
metadata:

  modified: 2026-09-02T18:12:49.419Z
---

While working in a git worktree, a later `cmake --build build/arm64` and a
`git status` ran in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin` (the main checkout)
instead of the worktree, so one build reported "no work to do" and a status
check looked as if every edit had been lost.

**Why:** After a `run_in_background` Bash call, and after a compound command
whose `cd` failed, the session cwd is the primary working directory again.
The tool result even says so, but it is easy to miss in a long session.

**How to apply:** In worktree sessions start every Bash command with
`cd <worktree> &&`, or use absolute paths everywhere (python patch scripts
with an absolute root are safest). Verify with `pwd` before trusting a
`git status` that looks wrong. See [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

name: workspace-harness-never-post-inits-on-mac
description: "On macOS the workspace adapter harness never reaches GUI_App::post_init; closing its frame crashes, so it exits via ExitMainLoop unless post_initialized()"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: ed4bbcf2-a467-44f4-bceb-b20f93cd25d8
  modified: 2026-09-17T16:28:53.409Z
---

Found 2026-09-17 while fixing the journey-tools branch (merged to jusprin-newui as 35eb1b4a59).

`tests/workspace/real_adapter_harness.cpp` does its work in one synchronous run. On macOS, Orca adds each web view's script handler from a CallAfter (`src/slic3r/GUI/Widgets/WebView.cpp`) that runs a script and waits on the page in a nested event loop. In this harness the first one never returns, so `is_adding_script_handler()` stays true, the later views pile up in the static `g_delay_webviews`, and `post_init` (gated on that flag in `GUI_App.cpp`) never runs, even if the harness waits for it (it times out at 180 s).

Closing the main frame ends that wait; the deferred view setup (use-after-free on destroyed views) and then `post_init` (on a destroyed frame) run and segfault (exit 139) after `HARNESS RESULT PASS`. The harness therefore closes the frame only when `post_initialized()` (true on Windows, where the handler is added synchronously) and otherwise calls `ExitMainLoop()`.

**Why:** a Windows fix switched the exit to `Close(true)` and made every macOS run crash; an Orca-side fix (drop destroyed views from `g_delay_webviews`) removed only one of the two crashes.

**How to apply:** if the workspace harness crashes on exit, look here first; don't make it wait for post_init. The shell harness is unaffected because its checks are asynchronous. Related: [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]], [[background-bash-timeout-kills-builds]].

name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-09-23T18:10:30.736Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. 37	
38	A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:
39	
40	```
41	cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
42	  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
43	  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
44	  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
45	  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
46	```
47	
48	CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.
49	
50	The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
51	without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
52	RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
53	reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
54	[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].
55	
56	FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
57	does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
58	(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
59	them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
60	created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
61	shown; web-view crashes vanish).
62	
63	`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
64	not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
65	--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
66	/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.
67	
68	CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
69	repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
70	`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
71	worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
72	"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
73	`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
74	absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
75	stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
76	(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
77	`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
78	paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.
79	
80	STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
81	rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
82	printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
83	wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
84	the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

86	name: liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit
87	description: "RelWithDebInfo liblibslic3r_gui.a crossed Apple ar's 4 GiB archive limit on jusprin-newui (2026-09-13); CMAKE_AR override is ignored; manual llvm-ar relink recipe and its cd trap"
88	metadata: 
89	  node_type: memory
90	  type: project
91	  originSessionId: 0771473f-5d46-4419-b8e5-112938ea6b34
92	  modified: 2026-09-14T14:18:50.456Z
93	---
94	
95	On 2026-09-13, at jusprin-newui 770bd2b0a2 (after "Add the evidence-led Add a
96	printer flow"), a worktree RelWithDebInfo build failed archiving
97	`src/slic3r/RelWithDebInfo/liblibslic3r_gui.a`:
98	`Assertion failed: (memberOffset < 0xFFFFFFFF) ... ArchiveWriter.cpp` then
99	`fatal error in .../ranlib`. The archive llvm-ar produced was 4,309,350,176
100	bytes; the main checkout's copy built minutes earlier was 4,143,827,796 and
101	still fit. Objects are big because the root CMakeLists.txt (lines ~544-548)
102	rewrites RelWithDebInfo -O2 to -O0 on purpose. Disk space was not the cause.
103	
104	**Why:** the failed build left the OLD harness binary in place, and the harness
105	runs afterwards "passed" against stale code (a new `--printer-setup` flag
106	silently ran the default mode: same 285 check count). Gate runs on build
107	success and compare binary mtime.
108	
109	**How to apply:**
110	- `-DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar` on an existing build dir does
111	  nothing: `CMakeFiles/<ver>/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` sets CMAKE_AR as a normal
112	  variable that shadows the cache.
113	- Working relink: `ninja -f build-RelWithDebInfo.ninja -t commands <target>`,
114	  drop compile lines, swap ar/ranlib for llvm-ar/llvm-ranlib on the gui archive
115	  line only, then run EACH line in its own `(cd build/arm64 && eval "$line")`.
116	  One `sh` script fails with bogus "no such file" errors because the
117	  encoding-check line does `cd src/slic3r` and it leaks; `sh -e` also does not
118	  stop inside `&&` chains. Apple's linker accepted the >4 GiB llvm-ar archive.
119	- The fix is PER BUILD DIRECTORY, nothing in the repo selects llvm-ar. Main
120	  checkout's build/arm64 cache has llvm-ar (commit 449b676145 documents it in
121	  agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md); any newly configured build dir
122	  gets Apple ar and fails again. Configure new dirs with the flags in
123	  [[jusprin-worktree-build]].
124	- Recurred 2026-09-14 on a fresh worktree at jusprin-newui bc19661a7f (archive
125	  4,308,513,464 bytes). Shortcut that worked: after the failed build, from
126	  `-t commands shell_integration_harness` drop lines containing ` -c `; only
127	  the last two remain relevant (gui archive, then harness link). Run just
128	  those two, swapping ar/ranlib on the archive line. Harness then passed.
129	- A lasting fix (llvm-ar in the toolchain, thin archives, or less debug info)
130	  is Kenneth's call; the main checkout will hit this on its next growth.
131	
132	Related: [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].

135	description: "A clean, merged, idle worktree under .claude/worktrees still belongs to its session; its owner can resume and check out over you mid-run. Always create your own."
136	metadata:
137	  node_type: memory
138	  type: feedback

142	
143	On 2026-09-23 I reused `.claude/worktrees/compassionate-gould-f98259` to skip a full build: it was clean, detached at a commit already merged into jusprin-newui, no process had files open there, and its build dir was only 9 days old. An hour later its owning session resumed, checked out two other branches there (the reflog shows it), rewrote ~13,800 resource files, and my running harness crashed with "Could not load bitmap: bed_high_templ" -- a symptom that looked like a product bug.
144	
145	**Why:** "clean and idle" says nothing about ownership. The session that created a worktree can resume at any time, and it has no way to know someone else moved in.
146	
147	**How to apply:** create a new worktree with its own name (`git worktree add -b <branch> .claude/worktrees/<name> <base>`) and configure a fresh build dir with the flags in [[jusprin-worktree-build]]. At jusprin-newui bd8ea51abc a fresh build of `jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs agent_bridge_tests shell_integration_harness` was 881 ninja steps, not the hour I feared. If a harness run dies strangely, check `git -C <worktree> reflog -3 --date=iso` and file mtimes before suspecting the code. Related: [[subagent-worktrees-create-manually]].

198	
199	`jusprin-newui` (the current working branch as of 2026-09-16) carries an in-process fake Bambu printer, landed as two commits: `7acf075aaa` (implementation, 2026-09-08 10:57) and `e04c0d40d3` (docs, 2026-09-08 11:00). Both are `Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>` — done by a Cursor agent on worktree branch `cursor/cd073db7` (created from `a9adaae973`), then cherry-picked onto `jusprin-newui` (parent `367f5703b3`). Operator guide: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md`.
200	
201	**Design:** unlike the Moonraker simulator ([[fake-moonraker-printer-sim]], which fakes the wire protocol and lives on a different branch entirely), this keeps a real Bambu Lab **system** preset selected (so `PresetBundle::is_bbl_vendor()` stays true and every Bambu-only UI gate passes) and substitutes only the printer-agent implementation, at the `NetworkAgentFactory` factory level, under id `jusprin-fake-bambu`. Two earlier attempts (`a162493544`, `3c244108b4`, both reverted same day) tried faking a *non-Bambu* agent or patching the header chip directly — both failed because Bambu-only gates rejected them or because it only patched a symptom. Faking Bambu's real network (MQTT/TLS 8883, FTPS 990, discovery) was evaluated and explicitly rejected as out of scope.
202	
203	**The seam:** exactly 4 added lines in `GUI_App::switch_printer_agent` (`src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_App.cpp:3574-3579`, 1 include + 3 body lines) — inside the existing `if (preset_bundle->is_bbl_vendor())` branch, `fake_bambu_printer_agent_id(app_config)` overrides `effective_agent_id` when fake mode is on, otherwise the branch is untouched. No upstream line deleted.
204	
205	**Config surface is a JSON file only, no MCP tools** (Kenneth's explicit call): turn it on via `"jusprin": {"fake_printer": true}` in `JusPrin2.conf` (JSON booleans store as the string `"true"`; an INI `[jusprin]` block is silently ignored), then drive live state by writing `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` (reread ~1s) with `state`/`progress`/`nozzle`/`bed`/`offline` keys. The C++ parameter carrying the datadir into the agent is misleadingly named `log_dir` (an upstream `NetworkAgentFactory::PrinterAgentFactory` convention, documented as "Directory for log files") — verified it's actually `data_dir()` at the call site, not a log subdirectory; don't be misled by the name when reading the code.
206	
207	Emulates printer type `N1` (`JUSPRIN_FAKE_BAMBU_PRINTER_TYPE`), device id `FAKE001`, shows as **JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)** in Select Machine. Idle/Printing/Offline is the printer-menu **first row** (opened by clicking the printer half of the chip), never on the chip itself. The heartbeat thread does not start in the constructor — only in `set_queue_on_main_fn` when a real callback is set — so unit tests that never wire that callback stay quiet. Test target: `jusprin_fake_bambu_tests` (`tests/jusprin/test_fake_bambu_agent.cpp`), coexists with `shell_theme_tests` in the same CMakeLists (their merge was a conflict the cherry-pick resolved by keeping both).

209	Doc pointers added in the two landing commits: `AGENTS.md`, `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md`, `agent-docs/jusprin/engineering-method.md` ("Printer tests without hardware" section), `agent-docs/jusprin/orca-integration-guide.md`. A planning handoff doc (`agent-docs/jusprin/fake-bambu-printer-handoff.md`) was never committed and doesn't exist in the tree — don't look for it.
210	
211	**Why:** Kenneth wants Bambu-path testing (header menu state, Select Machine, print job) without hardware, on the branch he actually works on day to day — distinct from the Moonraker/Klipper simulator, which stays on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` and covers the print-host HTTP path instead.

213	**How to apply:** For "fake a printer on jusprin-newui" requests, this is the one that's actually there — check `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/` first. 216	description: "A run_in_background Bash build dies at the tool timeout (ninja prints \"interrupted by user\", exit 130); launch long builds with nohup and watch the log instead"
217	metadata: 
218	  node_type: memory
219	  type: feedback
220	  originSessionId: 8c1e8dd3-1475-48e9-9398-2d5eaa424bab
221	  modified: 2026-09-14T19:01:34.576Z
222	---
223	
224	A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
225	bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
226	build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
227	which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
228	725-step JusPrin rebuild.
229	
230	**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
231	error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
232	compiled at all.
233	
234	**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
235	(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
236	then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
237	`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
238	[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

263	name: workspace-harness-never-post-inits-on-mac
264	description: "On macOS the workspace adapter harness never reaches GUI_App::post_init; closing its frame crashes, so it exits via ExitMainLoop unless post_initialized()"
265	metadata: 
266	  node_type: memory
267	  type: project
268	  originSessionId: ed4bbcf2-a467-44f4-bceb-b20f93cd25d8
269	  modified: 2026-09-17T16:28:53.409Z
270	---
271	
272	Found 2026-09-17 while fixing the journey-tools branch (merged to jusprin-newui as 35eb1b4a59).
273	
274	`tests/workspace/real_adapter_harness.cpp` does its work in one synchronous run. On macOS, Orca adds each web view's script handler from a CallAfter (`src/slic3r/GUI/Widgets/WebView.cpp`) that runs a script and waits on the page in a nested event loop. In this harness the first one never returns, so `is_adding_script_handler()` stays true, the later views pile up in the static `g_delay_webviews`, and `post_init` (gated on that flag in `GUI_App.cpp`) never runs, even if the harness waits for it (it times out at 180 s).
275	
276	Closing the main frame ends that wait; the deferred view setup (use-after-free on destroyed views) and then `post_init` (on a destroyed frame) run and segfault (exit 139) after `HARNESS RESULT PASS`. The harness therefore closes the frame only when `post_initialized()` (true on Windows, where the handler is added synchronously) and otherwise calls `ExitMainLoop()`.
277	
278	**Why:** a Windows fix switched the exit to `Close(true)` and made every macOS run crash; an Orca-side fix (drop destroyed views from `g_delay_webviews`) removed only one of the two crashes.
279	
280	**How to apply:** if the workspace harness crashes on exit, look here first; don't make it wait for post_init. The shell harness is unaffected because its checks are asynchronous. Related: [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]], [[background-bash-timeout-kills-builds]].

288	  modified: 2026-09-23T18:10:30.736Z
289	---
290	
291	Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.
292	
293	**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.
294	
295	The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.
296	
297	**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.
298	
299	**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].
300	
301	**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
302	2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
303	`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
304	`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
305	app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
306	a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
307	on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
308	the harness had opened on the Acer.
309	
310	Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
311	(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
312	captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
313	not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
314	"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.
315	
316	The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
317	read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
318	and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
319	evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
320	being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
321	concluding anything about the app.
322	
323	**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
324	`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
325	(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
326	`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
327	the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.
328	
329	**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
330	`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
331	`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
332	all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
333	directory — the directory alone is not enough.
334	
335	**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.
336	
337	**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.
338	
339	**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.
340	
341	**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
342	against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
343	first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
344	agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
345	had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
346	`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
347	all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
348	treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
349	`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
350	rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.
351	
352	**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
353	"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
354	reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
355	display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
356	sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
357	button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
358	until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].

result.output:
# 2. The surfaces that must remain

## 2.0 Project-window hierarchy

The Project window should not treat Prepare, Preview, and Info as three equal destinations.

- **Prepare is the dominant, persistent workspace.** It is where users inspect the model, communicate intent, manipulate geometry, resolve uncertainty, and review the agent's plan.
- **Check print opens Orca Preview in a modal window.** Prepare remains underneath; closing Check returns focus to Prepare. It is a secondary action when the active plate has a valid slice.
- **Info becomes Project details.** It is a drawer opened from the project name or menu. The agent reads its contents continuously even when the drawer is closed.
- **Print opens Send preflight.** It never sends directly. Explicit Send remains the consequential commitment.

The normal flow is:

`Prepare -> Check print -> return to Prepare if correction is needed -> Print -> Send preflight -> explicit Send`

### Default Project-window composition

The default window should contain:

- Project name and saved/unsaved state
- Compact printer pointer: target printer, nozzle, build plate, and material
- Compact, editable intent summary
- Compact active plate/object summary
- 3D Prepare canvas
- Essential direct-manipulation tools
- Compact pinned agent plan
- Highest unresolved assumption, compromise, or risk
- Check print
- Print
- Consequential warnings when applicable

The canvas is the primary human-agent collaboration surface. It must make the build plate and model visible, support camera rotation, pan, zoom, selection, and direct spatial manipulation, and show the changes the agent makes.

The compact summaries should keep the governing assumptions visible without expanding full editors. Examples:

> Decorative · appearance first · protect front surface · under 5 hours

> Plate 1 · Fuzzy Heart · 1 copy · PLA Matte

A one-object project should not permanently display a large object tree. A complete intent questionnaire should not remain expanded after it has been answered.

### Direct resolution of uncertainty
......
## 2.9 Print preflight

This surface answers: **Is the correct job about to be sent to the correct physical machine?**

Prepare should contain a visible Print entry point. Print opens this preflight; it does not bypass it:

`Print -> Send preflight -> explicit Send`

The current Print action opens Orca's existing Select Machine or printer-host send dialog, which requires a separate send/upload choice. The complete JusPrin preflight checklist below remains future product work.

### What should remain

- Job name and thumbnail
- Destination printer
- Selected plate
- Time and material estimate
- Filament and AMS mapping
- Plate-type confirmation
- Bed-leveling choice
- Flow-calibration choice
- Timelapse choice
- First-layer inspection
- Build-plate detection
- Tangle and clumping detection
- AI-monitoring behavior and sensitivity
- Recovery options
- Warnings about disabled checks
- Explicit Send control
......
## 2.12 Privacy, updates, portability, and expert administration

These functions are used less frequently, but they are important for particular users and organizations.

### User-owned decisions

- Cloud login region
- Stealth or offline mode
- Network-plugin use
- Preset synchronization
- Multi-device management
- Firmware and application update timing
- Camera and monitoring privacy
- Backup and recovery policy
- Importing and replacing configurations
- Ownership and export of project data

### Capabilities that should remain available

- Import 3MF, STL, STEP, SVG, OBJ, AMF, ZIP archives, and configurations
- Export models, projects, sliced plates, G-code, and preset bundles
- Export printer, filament, and process profiles
- Manage downloaded and stored printer files
- Access timelapses
- Run network diagnostics
- Open configuration data
- Enable developer tools

### Why the agent cannot decide these alone

These choices affect privacy, compatibility, organizational policy, intellectual property, and the user’s ability to leave the product.

The agent can simplify the workflows, but it should not silently enable cloud communication, install firmware, replace profiles, or trap projects in a proprietary format.

---

# 3. Recommended final product structure
......
## 3.5 Overlays and application-level layers

- **Send preflight:** final job, destination, material mapping, safety, and monitoring confirmation followed by explicit Send
- **Expert layer:** raw process settings, numeric per-object and per-region overrides, manual calibration ranges, toolpath diagnostics, and G-code
- **Preferences:** cloud region, stealth/offline behavior, network plugins, sync, updates, privacy, backup and recovery, import/export administration, and developer tools

This structure preserves the lifecycle of a print without turning Setup, Intent, Plan, Verify, Print, Monitor, and Diagnose into nine equal screens.

---

# 4. Visibility hierarchy

## 4.1 Default

Continuously visible in the ordinary Project window:

- Project name and saved/unsaved state
- Current printer, nozzle, plate, and material summary
- Compact intent summary
- Compact active plate and object summary
- 3D Prepare canvas
- Add, remove, select, move, rotate, scale, place on face, arrange, duplicate, Undo, and Redo
- Compact agent plan
- Highest unresolved assumption or risk
- Check print and Print

Inside Check, the default changes to sliced appearance, time, material, cost, the highest-priority warning, and comparison with intent. When supports exist, support placement and removal risk become the default Check emphasis.

## 4.2 Contextual

Shown when the project or current task makes it relevant:

- Full object, part, and plate tree
- Per-object material or extruder
- Modifiers, support enforcers, blockers, print order, and search
- Local surface annotations and object-specific requirements
- Mirror, cut, split, merge, assemble, text, measure, repair, positive/negative parts, and multi-plate distribution
- Seam, bridge, overhang, thin-feature, first-layer, island, and collision inspection
- Material changes, purge waste, prime tower, and extruder assignments
- Time and material estimate in Prepare after a valid background slice exists
- Assembly instructions, accessories, and reference pictures
- Calibration and maintenance recommendations
- Firmware updates, storage, timelapses, and multi-device management

## 4.3 On demand

Available through Project details, More, or the expert layer:

- Full intent questionnaire after it has been completed
- Project description, author, license, pictures, BOM, assembly guide, and profile notes
- Version, backup, ownership, and export administration
- Detailed agent rationale, alternatives, confidence, profile deviations, and change history
- Individual speeds and accelerations
- Exact line widths
- Infill and support implementation parameters
- Retraction, wiping, cooling, and purge details
- Complete toolpath legend and playback
- Raw G-code
- Manual calibration ranges
- Network tests, configuration folders, developer mode, and visualization preferences

## 4.4 Interruptive

Normally hidden, but presented prominently at the point where the user can resolve it:

- Wrong printer, nozzle, plate, or filament
- Safety or usage instruction relevant to the current plan
- Unsupported, missing, or defective geometry
- Support entering a protected region
- Violated dimensional requirement
- Material incompatible with the stated use
- Agent uncertainty about a meaning-changing geometry operation
- License conflict during sharing, publishing, commercial use, or export
- Unsaved work, recovery issue, or version conflict
- Printer-health or safety alert

# Inventory of OrcaSlicer notice kinds

Appendix to `investigation-print-issues-four-gaps.md`. Untracked on purpose.

Source: the `NotificationType` enum in `src/slic3r/GUI/NotificationManager.hpp` at `jusprin-newui` commit `570e3fb1c7` (62 kinds plus the count sentinel), and a search of every caller of the notification manager's `push_*` and `bbl_show_*` functions in `src/slic3r` (102 call sites outside the manager itself). "Lasting" means OrcaSlicer keeps the notice until it closes it itself; a number is the seconds before it fades. "JusPrin today" was checked by searching the fork's own code for any use of the notification manager: there is none except the file-load hook, so anything not listed as shown is shown nowhere while the shell is installed.

Route is my proposed classification:

- **Issue**: a print problem; belongs in the print-issue list.
- **Toast**: the result of something the person just did; a short-lived JusPrin confirmation.
- **Progress**: long-running work with a cancel; belongs with slicing progress in the header.
- **App**: application or account state; belongs on Home or in Preferences, not in a project.
- **None**: not shown.

## Print problems (states that can be asked again)

| Kind | Pushed by | Lasting? | Action on the notice | JusPrin today | Route |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ValidateError` | `Plater` after `Print::validate` (2 sites) | Lasting | "Jump to [object] (setting)" | Issue list | Issue (covered) |
| `ValidateWarning` | `Plater` (1 site) | Lasting | Same | Issue list | Issue (covered) |
| `SlicingError` | `Plater` when a slice fails; `GLCanvas3D` for path outside the plate, path above the height, and its generic errors | Lasting | "Jump to [object]" | Issue list | Issue (covered). Shared between producers |
| `SlicingSeriousWarning` | `GLCanvas3D`, G-code path conflict | Lasting | "Jump to [object]" | Issue list | Issue (covered) |
| `SlicingWarning` | `Plater`, slicing step warnings | Lasting | "Jump to [object]" | Issue list | Issue (covered) |
| `PlaterError` | `GLCanvas3D` (copy over the edge, SLA supports outside); `Plater::validate_current_plate`; `Plater.cpp` near line 15446 (mesh boolean failed during export); `GUI_ObjectList.cpp` 3292 (mesh combine failed) | Lasting | None | Edge case only | Issue for the edge; the two mesh failures are operation errors with no surface. Shared between producers |
| `LeftExtruderUnprintableError`, `RightExtruderUnprintableError` | `GLCanvas3D` and `Plater::validate_current_plate` | Lasting | "Click here to regroup" (opens the nozzle mapping dialog) | Issue list (words only) | Issue (covered; the action is lost) |
| `PlaterWarning` | `GLCanvas3D` (prime tower outside, filament mixture, "Only the object being edited is visible", object limited); `Plater.cpp` 17964; `GLGizmoMeshBoolean.cpp` (3 warnings from the boolean tool) | Lasting. Several at once, told apart by text | None | Prime tower and mixture only | Issue for those two; the rest have no surface. Shared between producers |
| `BBLFlushingVolumeZero` | `GLCanvas3D` | Lasting | "Flushing Volume" (opens the dialog) | **Nowhere** (problem 2) | Issue |
| `BBLFilamentPrintableError` | `GLCanvas3D` | Lasting | "Click here to regroup" | Issue list | Issue (covered) |
| `BBLSliceLimitError` | `GLCanvas3D`, after slicing | Lasting | "Click here to regroup" | Issue list | Issue (covered) |
| `BBLSliceMultiExtruderHeightOutside` | `GLCanvas3D`, after slicing | Lasting | None | Issue list | Issue (covered) |
| `BBLBedFilamentIncompatible` | `GLCanvas3D`, after slicing | Lasting | "Click for more." (wiki) | Issue list | Issue (covered) |
| `BBLMixUsePLAAndPETG` | `GLCanvas3D` | Lasting | "Click Wiki for help." | Issue list | Issue (covered) |
| `BBLNozzleFilamentIncompatible` | `GLCanvas3D` | Lasting | None | Issue list | Issue (covered) |
| `BBLSeqPrintInfo` | `Plater::config_change_notification` ("Print By Object: suggest auto-arrange") | 10 days | None | Nowhere | Toast, or drop: it is advice |
| `BBLSliceEmptyLayer`, `BBLNeedSupportON`, `BBLGcodeOverlap` | No caller in this version; the functions exist | n/a | None | n/a | Issue if upstream starts calling them |

## Results of something the person just did (events)

| Kind | Pushed by | Lasting? | Action | JusPrin today | Route |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ExportFinished` | `Plater` export paths (4 sites, including "sent to the printer's storage") and `push_import_finished_notification` ("Model file downloaded.") | 20 s; lasting when written to a removable drive | Open containing folder; Eject | Nowhere. The header's "Export sliced file…" ends with no confirmation | Toast with Open folder and Eject |
| `ExportOngoing` | `Plater`, 1 s after an export starts | Until the export ends | None | Nowhere | Progress |
| `CustomNotification` | 16 sites: drive ejected or eject failed (`Plater`), calibration INFO lines (`Plater`), bundle updated, downloaded, removed, no longer available, unauthorized (`GUI_App`, 9 sites), "Syncing presets from cloud…" (`MainFrame`), malformed download URL (`Downloader`), SLA archive without presets (`SLAImportJob`), objects that did not fit an arrange (`ArrangeJob`) | 10 s; errors lasting | None | Only those raised during a file load, which the file-load hook sends to the chat | Toast. One kind for unrelated facts, so it cannot be routed more finely |
| `BBLPlateInfo` | `ArrangeJob`, `OrientJob`: "This plate is locked", "No arrangeable objects are selected", "Object has zero size" | 10 days | None | Nowhere. An arrange that is refused looks like nothing happened | Toast |
| `ArrangeOngoing` | `ArrangeJob` | Until the job ends | None | Nowhere | Progress |
| `BBLGeneralError` | `Plater.cpp` 15476 and 15543, mesh combine failures | Lasting | None | Nowhere | Toast (error) |
| `CgalFinished` | `GUI_ObjectList`, repair finished | 5 s | None | Nowhere, unless the agent's repair tool reports it | Toast |
| `CustomSupportsAndSeamRemovedAfterRepair` | `Plater` (paint removed before repair); `GLGizmosManager` reuses it for "Error: Please close all toolbar menus first" | 10 s | None | Nowhere | Toast |
| `UpdatedItemsInfo` | `GUI_ObjectList`, cut connectors | 10 s | None | Nowhere | Toast |
| `EmptyColorChangeCode` | The layer slider in Check print | 10 s | None | Nowhere | Toast |
| `MmSegmentationExceededExtrudersLimit` | The colour painting tool | 10 s | None | Nowhere | Toast |
| `UnknownFont` | The text tool | Varies | None | Nowhere | Toast |
| `BBL3MFInfo` | `Plater` while loading a 3MF | 10 days | None | Chat, through the file-load hook | Covered |
| `BBLPreviewOnlyMode` | `Plater`, a G-code-only file was loaded | Lasting | None | Nowhere | Toast or a header state |

## Long-running work

| Kind | Pushed by | Lasting? | Action | JusPrin today | Route |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `SlicingProgress` | `Plater` | While slicing | Cancel; export link when done | Header | Covered |
| `ProgressIndicator` | The `Plater`'s job worker (arrange, orient, repair and the other background jobs) | While a job runs | Cancel | Nowhere: job progress and its Cancel are invisible | Progress |
| `PrintHostUpload` | `PrintHostDialogs.cpp`, one per upload to a network printer | Until done; errors stay | Cancel; error state | Nowhere | Progress. Better read from the upload queue's own public events (`EVT_PRINTHOST_PROGRESS`, `_ERROR`, `_CANCEL`) than from the notice |
| `URLDownload` | `Downloader` | Until done | Pause, cancel, open | Nowhere | Progress. `Downloader`'s public events carry the same facts |

## Application and account state

| Kind | Pushed by | Lasting? | Action | JusPrin today | Route |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `NewAppAvailable` | Call commented out in `GUI_App`; one wrapper with no caller | 20 s | Download page | n/a | None |
| `PresetUpdateAvailable` | `PresetUpdater` | 10 days | "Detail." | Nowhere | App |
| `PresetUpdateFinished` | `PresetUpdater` | 20 s | None | Nowhere | App |
| `BBLPluginUpdateAvailable` | `PresetUpdater` (2 sites) | 10 days | "Details" | Nowhere | App |
| `BBLPrinterConfigUpdateAvailable` | `PresetUpdater` | 10 days | "Details" | Nowhere | App |
| `BBLPluginInstallHint` | `Plater`, network plug-in not detected | Lasting | "Click here to install it." | The printer setup chat explains the missing plug-in when asked | App |
| `BBLUserPresetExceedLimit` | `GUI_App` | 10 days | "Wiki Guide" | Nowhere | App |
| `OrcaSharedProfilesAvailable` | `Plater` | Lasting | Browse; don't show again | Nowhere | App, or None |
| `OrcaSyncConflict` | `GUI_App`, preset sync conflict | Lasting | Two buttons: pull, or force push (delete in one case) | Nowhere. The conflict cannot be resolved while the shell is installed | App. The two actions live in a notice subclass, not in the generic link |
| `DidYouKnowHint` | `GUI_App` at start when hints are on | 300 s | Next and previous tip | Nowhere | None (decision) |
| `Mouse3dDisconnected` | `Mouse3DController` | 10 s | None | Nowhere | Toast or None |
| `DesktopIntegrationSuccess`, `UndoDesktopIntegrationSuccess` | The Linux desktop integration dialog | 10 s | None | Nowhere | None |
| `BBLObjectInfo` | `Plater` (2 sites): the object size card; with "(Repair)" when the mesh has open edges | 10 days | "(Repair)" | Nowhere | Decision: the open-edges case is a defective-geometry fact |
| `SimplifySuggestion` | The simplify tool, for very large meshes | 10 s | "Simplify model" | Nowhere | Toast or None |

## Declared but never pushed in this version

`NewAlphaAvailable`, `NewBetaAvailable`, `ProgressBar`, `EmptyAutoColorChange`, `SignDetected` (closed in one place, pushed nowhere), `QuitSLAManualMode` (referenced by the SLA tool only), `DesktopIntegrationFail`, `UndoDesktopIntegrationFail`, `OrcaCloudAPIError`.

## What upstream has added since the fork base

Fork base `3ffb9585d2` (2026-06-18), upstream `b3490a1cdc` (2026-10-09):

- 6 new kinds: `BBLSingleExtruderMixedFilamentRisk` and `BBLMixedFilamentBroken` (print problems), and four plug-in errors (`OrcaCloudPluginMissingError`, `OrcaLocalPluginMissingError`, `OrcaPluginInactiveError`, `OrcaPluginCapabilityUnavailableError`).
- 1 new canvas warning: `GLCanvas3D::EWarning::SingleExtruderMixedFilament`.
- Call sites that push a notice: 102 at the fork base, 125 upstream now. 19 of the 23 new ones are plain `push_notification(...)` calls, which add no enum value.
- The two enums were each touched by 15 upstream commits in the last two years.
